question: Which preregistered biological consciousness theory tests could justify transfer to nonbiological systems without subjective-experience ground truth?

sources.primary_type: preregistered adversarial multimodal human neuroscience study
sources.grade: E2 primary main Methods/Results/Discussion; supplements/raw not independently reanalyzed
sources.positive: Some sustained occipitotemporal representations and frontal–early-visual content synchronization
sources.negative: Specific posterior sustained synchrony and PFC offset-ignition predictions challenged
sources.limits: One coordinated experiment, suprathreshold task; cortical implementation tests, not AI subjective ground truth

sources.primary_type: Masked-visual EEG report versus no-report study
sources.grade: E2 original main Methods/Results/Discussion; OSF raw/analyses not rerun
sources.positive: Fronto-central N2 250–290 ms bifurcation in no-report condition
sources.negative: P3b more report-sensitive; N170 did not clearly bifurcate
sources.limits: No no-report trialwise subjective labels; covert judgments possible; sample size and mask subtraction constraints

sources.primary_type: Four-species fMRI anaesthesia/integration study with original model analyses
sources.grade: E2 original main Results/Methods/Discussion; underlying data, supplements and models not rerun

units.marmoset: 48 scans from four animals per condition

sources.positive: Phi_R generally declined under anaesthesia and responded to thalamic stimulation in macaques
sources.negative: Older Phi_2008 was unchanged or increased under some anaesthetics and species
sources.limits: Unresponsiveness not direct consciousness absence; fMRI physiology, pairwise approximation, nested runs and model assumptions
